segments.text: Every small business runs on routines nobody ever wrote down. FlowSME watches one round of the work, and hands back the process, the SOP, and the automation.

Hiring a consultant to shadow your staff is slow and expensive, so most small firms never do it. The same invoice gets retyped by hand, every day. This demo shows what we built during the hackathon, on Meta's models.

Here's a five-and-a-half-minute screen video of invoice entry: Notepad into an Excel tracker, explained out loud while working. Customers send a video like this from FlowSME Recorder, our Windows app, and the analysis runs on our server.

On the server, Muse Spark reads each screen change: which app, which field, and whether a value was typed, copied or pasted. Muse Voice Transcribe turns the soundtrack into text, lined up with the steps. Then Muse Spark names the tasks and writes the recommendations, as schema-checked JSON.

A couple of minutes later, the report is back. It found the same five-step routine four times, and six hours a month to save. The chart and the roadmap say what to automate first: a quick win that pays back in under seven months.
It also listens. The person said all their suppliers are on net 30, so the top recommendation works out the due date as the invoice date plus thirty days, instead of someone doing the sum.
For the team, there's a draft SOP: numbered steps with a screenshot of each, the checks, and an approval block. For whoever builds it, user stories with acceptance tests.
Build writes the workflow for the customer's own tool: n8n, Node-RED, Make, Power Automate, Logic Apps, or Windmill. The Recorder can send it there, switched off.

With the Recorder, only the active window goes to Meta. Every report has a spending cap, and employees see hours, never pay rates. FlowSME: show it the work once, and get the process and the automation.
